name: Almond Pudding No. 1
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: heaping tablespoonfuls of sifted flour
ingredients.originalText: two heaping tablespoonfuls of sifted flour

instructions.text: Put two quarts of milk into a double boiler
Stir into it two heaping tablespoonfuls of sifted flour that has been stirred to a cream, with a little of the milk
When it boils, care should be taken that it does not burn
When cooked, take from the fire and let it cool
Take the skins off from two pounds of sweet almonds, pound them fine, stir them into the milk
Add a teaspoonful of salt, a cupful of sugar, flavoring and six well-beaten eggs, the yolks and whites beaten separately
Put bits of butter over the top

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Put two quarts of milk into a double boiler
2. Stir into it two heaping tablespoonfuls of sifted flour that has been stirred to a cream, with a little of the milk
3. When it boils, care should be taken that it does not burn
4. When cooked, take from the fire and let it cool
5. Take the skins off from two pounds of sweet almonds, pound them fine, stir them into the milk
6. Add a teaspoonful of salt, a cupful of sugar, flavoring and six well-beaten eggs, the yolks and whites beaten separately
7. Put bits of butter over the top
8. Bake one hour
